RedFrontier
What we developed:RedFrontier is an end-to-end geospatial terrain intelligence and astronaut route-planning pipeline for Jezero Crater on Mars. It integrates regional 20m CTX (Context Camera) digital elevation models with ultra-high-resolution 1m HiRISE topography and confidence rasters. The system processes terrain slopes, local surface roughness, and sensor reliability to build a 60m navigation grid coupled with a life-support-constrained A* routing engine, exporting web-ready PNG map overlays, bounding-box metadata (layers.json), and navigable traverse paths (routes.geojson).

How it addresses the challenge:
RedFrontier translates raw orbital science datasets into actionable surface navigation. By enforcing boot-scale slope passability limits, Tobler-style metabolic walking penalties, and 8-hour suit oxygen and walk-back survivability budgets, it computes three distinct EVA traverse options (Fastest, Balanced, and Safest) tailored for mission safety and science exploration.

Why it is important:
Future astronauts on Mars will operate without GPS or real-time Earth guidance. RedFrontier equips mission planners and human explorers with transparent, hazard-aware mapping to plan and execute safe, scientifically productive Marswalks in extreme planetary terrain.
details:
Project Details: RedFrontier

What It Does & How It Works

RedFrontier is an interactive Martian surface navigation and Extravehicular Activity (EVA) planning platform designed for Jezero Crater. It fuses multi-resolution NASA orbital datasets—specifically regional 20 m/pixel CTX (Context Camera) digital elevation models and ultra-high-resolution 1 m/pixel HiRISE (High Resolution Imaging Science Experiment) topography and Figure of Merit (FOM) confidence maps—into an integrated, layered decision-support system.

Under the hood, RedFrontier operates as a two-stage geospatial and pathfinding pipeline:

  1. Multi-Scale Terrain & Reliability Processing: Using latitude-corrected spherical trigonometry for Mars, the engine computes surface slope (in degrees) and local terrain roughness across multi-gigabyte GeoTIFF rasters in memory-safe blocks. It cross-references HiRISE elevation data with sensor FOM confidence classes to penalize noisy or interpolated terrain, generating composite hazard maps.
  2. Life-Support-Constrained A Routing:* The pipeline aggregates terrain metrics onto a 60 m navigation grid and applies a custom cost function incorporating Tobler-style slope-dependent walking speeds ($2\text{ km/h}$ flat baseline), boot-scale slope limits ($12.5^\circ$ at 20 m scale, approximating $\sim20^\circ$ at human boot scale), and an 8-hour suit oxygen reserve budget (including a 25% safety margin and 1-hour science dwell time). For any selected start and science target, it computes three distinct routes—Fastest, Balanced, and Safest—and exports web-ready PNG overlays (layers.json) and GeoJSON paths (routes.geojson) for interactive web visualization.

Key Benefits & Intended Impact

  • Astronaut Safety & Survival Assurance: Automatically verifies round-trip walk-back feasibility against suit oxygen limits before an astronaut ever steps onto the terrain, eliminating dead-end traverses or unwalkable steep slopes.
  • Actionable Data Fusion: Translates massive, raw scientific GeoTIFF datasets (hundreds of millions of grid cells) into lightweight, browser-ready visual layers (hillshade relief, slope, roughness, blocked zones, and sensor reliability) that load instantaneously on mission consoles.
  • Intended Impact: Unlike Earth, Mars has no GPS constellation or real-time ground control due to communication delays. RedFrontier empowers future human explorers and mission planners to autonomously plan safe, efficient, and scientifically rich Marswalks—bridging the gap between orbital reconnaissance and boots-on-the-ground planetary exploration.

Tools, Languages, Hardware & Software Used

  • Programming Languages: Python (geospatial backend & routing engine), HTML5/CSS3/JavaScript (interactive web mapping interface).
  • Core Python Libraries: rasterio and GDAL (windowed GeoTIFF processing & coordinate transformations), pyproj (Martian Equirectangular projection math using Mars radius $R = 3,396,190\text{ m}$), NumPy and SciPy (Gaussian smoothing, distance transforms, and statistical terrain aggregation), scikit-image (route_through_array graph pathfinding), and Matplotlib (colormap rendering and hillshade generation).
  • NASA Datasets: Mars 2020 Jezero Crater CTX 20 m DEM, MOLA-aligned HiRISE 1 m DTM mosaics, and HiRISE FOM Confidence rasters.
  • Development Environment: Google Colab / Jupyter Notebooks (cloud compute for large raster processing) and web mapping frameworks (Leaflet / GeoJSON rendering).

How RedFrontier Is Creative

Rather than treating Martian elevation maps as static visual backgrounds, RedFrontier treats terrain uncertainty and human physiology as first-class routing variables. By combining orbital data confidence scores (penalizing low-FOM areas where stereo reconstruction is noisy) with sub-grid slope maxima (catching sharp 20 m cliffs hidden inside smoother 60 m cells) and metabolic oxygen budgets, it transforms passive satellite imagery into a dynamic "survival co-pilot."

Key Factors Our Team Considered

  • Scale Discrepancy ("Sub-Pixel Cliffs"): A 60 m grid cell might appear gentle on average while hiding a dangerous $25^\circ$ drop-off at 20 m or 1 m resolution. We explicitly tracked maximum sub-cell slopes (slopemax60) and blocked cells where over 30% of sub-pixels exceeded safe thresholds.
  • Data Reliability vs. Terrain Hazard: Orbital DTMs contain artifacts and interpolated patches (FOM class 15 or low-confidence classes 1–11). We factored sensor uncertainty directly into the hazard cost so routes naturally favor well-mapped, high-confidence ground.
  • Human Life-Support Margins: Every route is evaluated not just on distance, but on total round-trip time plus science station dwell time against a strict 75% usable oxygen ceiling (reserving 25% for emergencies).
  • Web Performance & Accessibility: Raw planetary GeoTIFFs exceed several gigabytes and cannot render in standard browsers. We engineered an automated tiling/overlay exporter (layers.json + transparent PNGs) so any mission dashboard can display high-resolution multi-layered terrain smoothly.
